name: NVIDIA
basis: each funding- or dividend-inclusive history is scaled to its own latest raw USD close

fundingForecast.displaySign: positive is earned by a perp long; negative is paid by a perp long

onchainSpot.preferenceBasis: all pages display separate CEX reported-volume and contract-backed DEX execution sections
onchainSpot.volumeSource: direct Binance, Bitget, Bybit, OKX, and Meteora venue APIs plus factory-verified PancakeSwap V3 pool-event volume indexed by DexScreener; DEX quote routes without indexed pool-event volume are excluded
onchainSpot.liquiditySource: direct CEX order books; direct Ethereum, Robinhood-chain, and PancakeSwap V3 quoter depth; direct Meteora pool state; and direct Jupiter executable round-trip quotes

peerMapping.justification: The block uses XYZ100 as the sole primary index hedge and nine positive-weight single-name peers that sum to exactly 1. The construction overweights direct AI accelerator competition, HBM and DRAM supply, and hyperscale AI demand, then adds adjacent data-center silicon. Liquidity is respected but not allowed to override comparability: INTC has 6.434 USD millions of displayed 24-hour perp liquidity yet stays small because its AI-GPU overlap is weaker, while AMZN has only 0.462 USD millions and is sized accordingly. All references preserve the displayed liquidity unit, USD millions.

peers.name: Advanced Micro Devices
peers.reason: Most direct single-name comparator in GPUs and AI accelerators, but its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity of 1.18 USD millions is below NVDA's 3.384 USD millions, so the weight is large but not dominant.

peers.name: Micron Technology
peers.reason: High-bandwidth memory and AI server memory exposure give strong NVDA supply-chain comparability, and its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity of 11.877 USD millions supports a large sleeve.

peers.name: Marvell Technology
peers.reason: Data-center interconnect, networking, and custom silicon exposure make it economically relevant to NVDA's AI systems cycle, with displayed 24-hour perp liquidity of 1.269 USD millions keeping the weight moderate.

peers.name: Intel
peers.reason: Semiconductor manufacturing, CPUs, and AI adjacency provide partial comparability; its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity of 6.434 USD millions is ample, but the business mix is less similar than AMD or MRVL.

peers.name: SK hynix common
peers.reason: SK hynix common adds HBM and advanced memory comparability with very deep 24-hour perp liquidity of 18.246 USD millions, so it is weighted close to MU.

peers.name: Alphabet
peers.reason: AI compute demand, TPU development, and data-center monetization create a customer-and-platform link to NVDA, with displayed 24-hour perp liquidity of 2.262 USD millions consistent with a medium weight.

peers.name: Microsoft
peers.reason: Microsoft represents hyperscale AI capital spending and accelerator demand; its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 1.386 USD millions, supporting a meaningful but not dominant weight.

peers.name: Amazon
peers.reason: Amazon is included for cloud AI capital spending and demand, but its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is only 0.462 USD millions, so the weight is kept smaller.

peers.name: Nebius Group
peers.reason: Nebius is an AI infrastructure and cloud capacity proxy rather than a chip supplier, so it receives the smallest weight despite 24-hour perp liquidity of 2.35 USD millions being reasonably close to NVDA's 3.384 USD millions.

primary_index_hedge.name: Nasdaq-100
primary_index_hedge.reason: Nasdaq-100 is the cleaner primary hedge for NVIDIA because it matches megacap technology, growth, and AI beta more closely than the broader S&P 500; XYZ100 shows 21.944 USD millions of displayed 24-hour perp liquidity versus 30.814 USD millions for SP500, so liquidity is sufficient while factor fit is better.

peerMapping.historyMethod: daily-rebalanced peer spot total returns using the fixed Kimi weights; unavailable pre-listing peers are omitted and remaining weights renormalized once at least three peers exist; the browser rebases the basket to the target spot level at the first shared date of each selected chart range

liveSplice.method: current TradeXYZ perp mid divided by that peer's TradeXYZ close on its latest spot date; available Kimi weights renormalized and applied as a one-period return from the published peer spot endpoint; USD cash close is retained for disclosure but never mixed with a differently scaled perp contract

earningsOptions.source: Schwab listed-options chain, FMP earnings calendars, and Sharadar adjusted prices

liquidityFilter.sides: OTM puts below spot and OTM calls above spot

model.name: liquid vertical-spread risk-neutral CDF
model.description: Liquid vertical spreads are used when the chain supplies at least four valid probability points; otherwise the nearest liquid ATM straddle supplies the expiration distribution. Earnings-date log distances are time-scaled from the first post-event expiration.
model.measure: risk-neutral, not a historical or physical forecast

historicalAnalysis.eventSource: SEC earnings release history with FMP historical calendar fallback
historicalAnalysis.method: Each current two-leg structure is translated into percentage-of-spot strikes and debit. Those same normalized strikes and today's debit percentage are replayed across prior earnings using the same calendar-day entry lead and post-event exit horizon. A profitable event requires expiration payoff greater than the original debit.
historicalAnalysis.limitation: Stock-path proxy using today's premium; historical option quotes, bid-ask execution, volatility repricing, early exercise, dividends, and transaction costs are not reconstructed.
